question: Which three exercises are described as making up the Basic Control Skills Test in Section 12 of the manual?
choice_a: Forward stop, straight-line backing, forward offset tracking
choice_b: Straight line backing, offset back/left, parallel park (conventional)
choice_d: Reverse offset tracking, roadside stop, lane change
explanation: The manual lists: "Straight line backing. Offset back/left. Parallel park (conventional)" as the exercises used to test basic control skills.
source_note: Arizona Commercial Driver License Manual (AAMVA 2005/2022 CDL Testing System, ADOT MVD, Revised 01/2026), Section 12 - Basic Control Skills Test, p. 12-1

question: How is an "encroachment" scored during the Basic Control Skills Test?
choice_a: Each time the vehicle stops without changing direction
choice_b: Each time any portion of the vehicle touches or crosses over an exercise boundary line or cone
choice_c: Each time the driver checks a mirror during backing
choice_d: Each time the vehicle exceeds the posted speed limit
explanation: The manual states the examiner "will score the number of times you touch or cross over an exercise boundary line or cone with any portion of your vehicle. Each encroachment will count as an error."
source_note: Arizona Commercial Driver License Manual (AAMVA 2005/2022 CDL Testing System, ADOT MVD, Revised 01/2026), Section 12 - Basic Control Skills Test, p. 12-1

question: What is a "pull-up" in Basic Control Skills Test scoring, and how are initial pull-ups treated?
choice_a: Backing further to correct position; it is always counted as an error
choice_b: Stopping and pulling forward to clear an encroachment or get a better position; the applicant will not be penalized for initial pull-ups
choice_c: Exiting the vehicle to look; it is always an automatic failure
choice_d: Crossing a boundary line; it is treated the same as an encroachment
explanation: The manual explains: "When a driver stops and pulls forward to clear an encroachment or to get a better position, it is scored as a 'pull-up.' ... You will not be penalized for initial pull-ups. However, an excessive number of pull-ups, will count as errors."
source_note: Arizona Commercial Driver License Manual (AAMVA 2005/2022 CDL Testing System, ADOT MVD, Revised 01/2026), Section 12 - Basic Control Skills Test, p. 12-1

question: In the Basic Control Skills Test described in Section 12, what is the maximum number of times an applicant may look to check the vehicle's position, and which exercise is the exception?
choice_a: Three times for all exercises, no exceptions
choice_b: Two times for all exercises except Straight Line Backing, which allows only one look
choice_c: Unlimited looks are allowed for all exercises
choice_d: One time for all exercises except Parallel Park, which allows two looks
explanation: The manual states: "The maximum number of times that you may look to check the position of your vehicle is two (2) except for the Straight Line Backing exercise, which allows one look."
source_note: Arizona Commercial Driver License Manual (AAMVA 2005/2022 CDL Testing System, ADOT MVD, Revised 01/2026), Section 12 - Basic Control Skills Test, p. 12-1

question: What are the four exercises included in the Modernized Basic Control Skills Test (Section 12M)?
choice_a: Forward Stop, Straight-Line Backing, Forward Offset Tracking, Reverse Offset Tracking
choice_b: Straight Line Backing, Offset Back/Left, Parallel Park, Alley Dock
choice_c: Forward Stop, Parallel Park, Lane Change, Railroad Crossing
choice_d: Reverse Offset Tracking, Urban Business, Expressway Merge, Curve
explanation: The manual states: "Exercise 1 - Forward Stop, Exercise 2 - Straight-Line Backing, Exercise 3 - Forward Offset Tracking, and Exercise 4 - Reverse Offset Tracking."
source_note: Arizona Commercial Driver License Manual (AAMVA 2005/2022 CDL Testing System, ADOT MVD, Revised 01/2026), Section 12M - Modernized Basic Control Skills Test, p. 12M-1

question: Under the Modernized Basic Control Skills Test, how many free looks are allowed on Exercise 2 (Straight-Line Backing) versus Exercise 4 (Reverse Offset Backing)?
choice_a: Zero on Exercise 2; one on Exercise 4
choice_b: One on Exercise 2; two on Exercise 4
choice_c: Two on Exercise 2; two on Exercise 4
choice_d: Three on Exercise 2; one on Exercise 4
explanation: The manual states: "You may be allowed a maximum of one (1) free look on Exercise 2 - Straight-line Backing, and two (2) free looks on Exercise 4 - Reverse Offset Backing, to check the position of your vehicle."
source_note: Arizona Commercial Driver License Manual (AAMVA 2005/2022 CDL Testing System, ADOT MVD, Revised 01/2026), Section 12M - Modernized Basic Control Skills Test, p. 12M-1

question: What must an applicant demonstrate during Exercise 1 (Forward Stop) of the Modernized Basic Control Skills Test?
choice_a: Backing the vehicle in a straight line through an alley
choice_b: Judging the front of the vehicle during a controlled stop, stopping with the front most part of the vehicle within the box without going past it
choice_c: Parking the vehicle parallel to a curb on the right
choice_d: Merging into expressway traffic while maintaining speed
explanation: The manual states: "You will demonstrate your ability to judge the front of your vehicle during a controlled stop. Drive forward through the alley and stop with the front most part of the vehicle within the box at the end of the alley without going past it. You may stop only once."
source_note: Arizona Commercial Driver License Manual (AAMVA 2005/2022 CDL Testing System, ADOT MVD, Revised 01/2026), Section 12M - Modernized Basic Control Skills Test, p. 12M-2

question: After completing an exercise such as Straight-Line Backing in the Modernized Basic Control Skills Test, what must the applicant do to signal completion to the examiner?
choice_a: Turn off the headlights and wave out the window
choice_b: Set the parking brake, shift to neutral, and sound the horn
choice_c: Exit the vehicle and stand beside it
choice_d: Flash the turn signals three times
explanation: The manual states: "When you have completed the exercise, set your parking brake, shift to neutral and sound your horn. This will inform the examiner you have completed the exercise and allow them to score your final position."
source_note: Arizona Commercial Driver License Manual (AAMVA 2005/2022 CDL Testing System, ADOT MVD, Revised 01/2026), Section 12M - Modernized Basic Control Skills Test, p. 12M-2

question: In Exercise 4 (Reverse Offset Tracking) of the Modernized Basic Control Skills Test, how close must the rear most part of the vehicle come to the rear of the alley?
explanation: The manual states the applicant should "offset back into the alley, bringing the rear most part of your vehicle within three (3) feet of the rear of the alley."
source_note: Arizona Commercial Driver License Manual (AAMVA 2005/2022 CDL Testing System, ADOT MVD, Revised 01/2026), Section 12M - Modernized Basic Control Skills Test, p. 12M-3

question: What could happen if an applicant opens the vehicle door while the vehicle is still moving during the Modernized Basic Control Skills Test?
choice_a: It only counts as one "look" with no other consequence
choice_b: It may result in an automatic failure for an unsafe act
choice_c: The examiner will pause the test and allow a restart
choice_d: It has no scoring impact as long as the vehicle stops immediately after
explanation: The manual warns: "If you open your door while the vehicle is moving (not in neutral and park), it may result in an automatic failure for an unsafe act."
source_note: Arizona Commercial Driver License Manual (AAMVA 2005/2022 CDL Testing System, ADOT MVD, Revised 01/2026), Section 12M - Modernized Basic Control Skills Test, p. 12M-1

question: When stopping for a railroad crossing (required for buses, school buses, or vehicles displaying placards), how far from the nearest rail must the vehicle stop?
choice_a: Within 50 feet but not less than 15 feet
choice_b: Within 100 feet but not less than 50 feet
choice_d: Within 25 feet but not less than 5 feet
explanation: The manual states: "Stop the vehicle within 50 feet but not less than 15 feet from the nearest rail."
source_note: Arizona Commercial Driver License Manual (AAMVA 2005/2022 CDL Testing System, ADOT MVD, Revised 01/2026), Section 13 - Road Test, p. 13-3

question: According to the road test criteria, when does "unsafe coasting" occur?
choice_b: When the vehicle is out of gear (clutch depressed or gearshift in neutral) for more than the length of the vehicle
choice_c: Anytime the driver shifts gears while turning
choice_d: When the parking brake is applied while the vehicle is moving
explanation: The manual states: "Unsafe coasting occurs when your vehicle is out of gear (clutch depressed or gearshift in neutral) for more than the length of your vehicle."
source_note: Arizona Commercial Driver License Manual (AAMVA 2005/2022 CDL Testing System, ADOT MVD, Revised 01/2026), Section 13 - Road Test, p. 13-1

question: Once the vehicle has come to a full stop during a roadside stop maneuver on the road test, which of the following is part of the required procedure?
choice_a: Leave the vehicle in gear with a foot on the brake
choice_b: Apply the parking brake, move the gear shift to neutral or park, and activate the four-way emergency flashers
choice_c: Immediately exit the vehicle without setting the parking brake
choice_d: Keep the turn signal on to indicate the stop is temporary
explanation: The manual lists, once stopped: "Activate your four-way emergency flashers. Apply the parking brake. Move the gear shift to neutral or park. Remove your feet from the brake and clutch pedals."
source_note: Arizona Commercial Driver License Manual (AAMVA 2005/2022 CDL Testing System, ADOT MVD, Revised 01/2026), Section 13 - Road Test, p. 13-2

question: According to the general driving behavior criteria for manual transmissions, what practice is required regarding shifting?
choice_a: Ride the clutch to control speed
choice_b: Double-clutch when shifting, without revving or lugging the engine
choice_c: Shift without using the clutch to save time
choice_d: Coast with the clutch depressed between gears
explanation: The manual states: "You must double-clutch when shifting. Do not rev or lug the engine. Do not ride clutch to control speed, coast with the clutch depressed, or 'pop' the clutch."
source_note: Arizona Commercial Driver License Manual (AAMVA 2005/2022 CDL Testing System, ADOT MVD, Revised 01/2026), Section 13 - Road Test, p. 13-3

question: During the road test, what might the examiner ask the applicant after the vehicle passes under an overpass or over a bridge?
choice_a: The applicant's opinion of the road surface quality
choice_b: The posted clearance/height (overpass) or the posted weight limit (bridge)
choice_c: The exact number of other vehicles on the bridge
choice_d: The construction date of the bridge
explanation: The manual states: "After driving under an overpass, you may be asked to tell the examiner what the posted clearance or height was. After going over a bridge, you may be asked to tell the examiner what the posted weight limit was."
source_note: Arizona Commercial Driver License Manual (AAMVA 2005/2022 CDL Testing System, ADOT MVD, Revised 01/2026), Section 13 - Road Test, p. 13-3

question: When stopping for a student discharge, how far from the students at the stop must the school bus come to a complete stop, per the road test criteria?
explanation: The manual states: "Bring school bus to a complete stop at least 10' away from students at the stop."
source_note: Arizona Commercial Driver License Manual (AAMVA 2005/2022 CDL Testing System, ADOT MVD, Revised 01/2026), Section 13 - Road Test, p. 13-3

topic: Regular Traffic Checks and Turn Signals
question: Per the general driving behavior scoring criteria on the road test, when must a driver check mirrors and traffic in relation to an intersection?
choice_b: Before, while in, and after an intersection
choice_c: Only if a pedestrian is visible
choice_d: Only when changing lanes near the intersection
explanation: The manual states: "Check mirrors and traffic before, while in and after an intersection," as part of the Regular Traffic Checks scoring category.
source_note: Arizona Commercial Driver License Manual (AAMVA 2005/2022 CDL Testing System, ADOT MVD, Revised 01/2026), Section 13 - Road Test, p. 13-4
